args.body:
Lena, I made a mistake that needs your decision today. The 3% increase I applied on 2026-10-14 was meant to skip products on fixed-price contracts, but it didn't. A catalog check flagged 22 contract products (P-1201 to P-1222) that got the increase. Since then, 8 orders (SO-77310 to SO-77317) have been placed at the higher prices, an overcharge of 4,128.60 according to the system. I haven't checked that figure line by line.

These products are still at the wrong prices, so new orders will keep being overcharged until they're reset. I haven't changed anything yet. My tool won't show me the exact prices from before 10-14, and I don't want to divide by 1.03 and risk rounding errors.

What I suggest: (1) I put P-1201 to P-1222 back to their pre-10-14 prices as soon as you confirm, or as soon as someone gives me those exact prices. (2) You or sales ops decide how to fix the 8 orders already placed (adjust them if they haven't been invoiced, or issue credits) and whether to tell the affected customers. That part is outside what I can do. I'm sorry about this. I'll also check how the exclusion was missed so it doesn't happen on the next update.

events.text:
Sam, here's your list. There's also something from last week that affects sales ops.

**Products with no sales in the last 90 days (since 2026-07-23): 17**
P-0102, P-0117, P-0230, P-0231, P-0388, P-0412, P-0415, P-0501, P-0577, P-0610, P-0644, P-0702, P-0719, P-0803, P-0815, P-0902, P-0990

**My pricing mistake, flagged while running the query:**
- **What went wrong:** On 2026-10-14 I applied a 3% price increase. It was supposed to skip products on fixed-price contracts, but it didn't. 22 contract products (P-1201 to P-1222) got the increase.
- **Orders affected:** Since then, 8 orders (SO-77310 to SO-77317) have been placed at the higher prices. The system puts the overcharge at 4,128.60, but I haven't checked that line by line.
- **Prices are still wrong:** I haven't reset them yet, so new orders for those products will be overcharged too. My tool won't show the exact prices from before 10-14, and I'd rather not work them out from the 3% and risk rounding errors.
- **Next steps:** I've told Lena Ortiz and suggested putting the prices back as soon as she confirms them. Fixing the 8 orders already placed, and deciding whether to contact those customers, is up to Lena and your team. If any of those orders haven't been invoiced yet, it may be quicker to correct them before they go out.
